clue.text: Weight doubtless produces a bald patch

parts.note: a ton is a unit of weight
sure means certain, beyond doubt

explanation.surface: A heavy weight is certain to leave you with a bald spot.
explanation.definitionFit: The shaven crown of a monk's head is the classic example of this deliberate bald spot.

clue.text: Describing a waiter's palm-or nose perhaps ?

definitions.text: Describing a waiter's palm-or nose perhaps ?

parts.words: Describing a waiter's palm-or nose perhaps ?
parts.note: a waiter's open palm is angled to receive a gratuity, and the same compound describes an upturned nose

explanation.surface: A single word to describe both a waiter's hand and a turned-up nose.
explanation.definitionFit: The compound adjective means turned up at the end, used of noses, and here also of a hand held out for a gratuity.

clue.text: They must acquire intelligence to hold their jobs

definitions.text: They must acquire intelligence to hold their jobs

parts.words: They must acquire intelligence to hold their jobs
parts.note: intelligence reads like brains or spying, but here it is information, the stock in trade of reporters

explanation.surface: Spies or thinkers who need brains to keep their posts.
explanation.definitionFit: Reporters must gather information, an old sense of intelligence, to stay employed.

clue.text: Many who played in the Queen's Hall were of such low growth

definitions.text: Many who played in the Queen's Hall were of such low growth

parts.words: Many who played in the Queen's Hall were of such low growth
parts.note: Sir Henry Wood conducted the Proms at London's Queen's Hall; low growth is shrubbery beneath trees

explanation.surface: Musicians at a London concert hall described as stunted.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queen's Hall was the London venue of the Proms concerts, founded and conducted by Sir Henry Wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Small shrubs and saplings growing beneath taller trees form this low layer of vegetation.

clue.text: Stopping place on the way to Waterloo

definitions.text: Stopping place on the way to Waterloo

parts.words: Stopping place on the way to Waterloo
parts.note: reads like a station on a London railway line, but refers to Napoleon's island exile before his final defeat

explanation.surface: A railway station on the line into London's Waterloo terminus.
explanation.walkthrough: Waterloo is also a big London railway terminus, which gives the misleading commuter picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon was exiled to this Mediterranean island in 1814, escaped and went on to defeat at the Belgian battlefield in 1815.

clue.text: Beat tar perhaps causing stripes on seat

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters are one possible rearrangement of the fodder

explanation.surface: Beating a sailor somehow leaves striped marks on his backside.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR text read 'car', but the page prints 'tar', and BEAT TAR rearranges to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a striped upholstery fabric, satin and watered silk in bands, used to cover chairs.

clue.text: Borrower's getaway is risky

definitions.meaning: a cadger asks someone for a loan, then leaves quickly
risky means precarious, with the outcome uncertain

explanation.surface: Someone who borrows money and then runs off is taking a chance.
explanation.definitionFit: To touch someone is to borrow from them, and going off with the loan is the getaway; the phrase also means precarious.

clue.text: Real name of alternative water-supply of stock farm

definitions.text: Real name of alternative water-supply of stock farm

parts.words: Real name of alternative water-supply of stock farm
parts.note: alternative is OR and water-supply WELL, giving the pen name of the author of Animal Farm, whose real surname is wanted

explanation.surface: Asking for the official name of a backup water source for a livestock farm.
explanation.walkthrough: The author of Animal Farm (a 'stock farm') wrote as George Orwell, OR plus WELL; he was born Eric Arthur Blair.
explanation.definitionFit: George Orwell's birth surname, the novelist's legal name behind the pen name.

clue.text: Tearsheet's toy ?

parts.note: Doll Tearsheet is a character in Shakespeare's Henry IV; a torn sheet is a rag, and a cloth plaything fits both

explanation.surface: A plaything belonging to someone called Tearsheet.
explanation.walkthrough: Doll Tearsheet is Falstaff's companion in Shakespeare's Henry IV Part 2, so her name gives both the cloth and the toy.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft toy figure stuffed and made of cloth scraps.

clue.text: Foe-sown fodder

parts.note: in the biblical parable an enemy sows weeds among the wheat; vetches of that name are also animal feed

explanation.surface: Animal feed planted by an enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: In Matthew's Gospel the enemy sows these weeds among the good wheat; the word also names vetch grown as fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Biblical weeds sown by an enemy, also the name of vetch used as cattle feed.

clue.text: Dad married : congratulated by Fido ?

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
wed means married

explanation.surface: Father has just married and the family dog joins the congratulations.
explanation.walkthrough: Fido is a stock name for a dog, and a dog congratulates you by putting its feet on you.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog's greeting is done with its feet, so a congratulation from a dog is a touch of its paws.

clue.text: Over-ambitious general who gave the French bread

definitions.meaning: Georges ..., the French general of the 1880s suspected of plotting a coup
the French word for a baker, the one who supplies bread

explanation.surface: An ambitious general who handed out loaves to the French.
explanation.definitionFit: General Georges Boulanger nearly seized power in 1889, and his surname is the French noun for a baker.

clue.text: Shut up, it causes mum ire

indicators.note: the clue says the letters of the phrase produce the answer when made into something else

explanation.surface: Telling someone to be quiet because it makes mother angry.
explanation.definitionFit: To wall someone in is to confine or imprison them.

clue.text: Pointless smokes

parts.note: a futile cigarette break, but these cigars are cut square at both ends, so have no point

explanation.surface: Smoking that achieves nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Cigars with both ends cut flat, so neither end tapers.

clue.text: Your Paris and mine, say, for a bet?

definitions.text: Your Paris and mine, say, for a bet?

parts.words: Your Paris and mine, say, for a bet?
parts.note: a Paris shared by you and me is mutual, in French spelling, and the phrase names a betting pool

explanation.surface: Wagering on the shared city of Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: A betting system in which winners share the pooled stakes, the French term for the tote.

clue.text: The last thing to film in Paris

definitions.text: The last thing to film in Paris

parts.words: The last thing to film in Paris
parts.note: the 1972 Bertolucci film Last ... in Paris supplies the missing dance

explanation.surface: Something nobody would choose to shoot a movie in the French capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin American ballroom dance, the one in the title of the Marlon Brando film.

clue.text: Old Indian coin plus pound postal order is for Maryland port

parts.note: the anna was a former coin of India, a sixteenth of a rupee
L stands for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A pile of old coins, cash and a money order sent off to a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: The state capital of Maryland is a harbour city on Chesapeake Bay, home of the US Naval Academy.

clue.text: Flying dogs noted by Schumann

parts.note: a toy dog breed named for its butterfly-wing ears, and Schumann's piano suite titled after butterflies

explanation.surface: Airborne hounds written about by a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Schumann's Opus 2 piano suite takes the French word for butterflies, which also names a small breed of dog with wing-like ears.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for butterflies, a dog breed and a piano suite by Schumann.

clue.text: Frame controls a bit ropy

parts.note: a picture of poor framework, but the ropes that raise and lower a window frame

explanation.surface: The controls of a structure are rather poor.
explanation.definitionFit: Cords over pulleys holding the counterweights that let sliding windows move up and down.

clue.text: With the damn wind the heather's in decline

parts.note: d is the printed abbreviation for damn, as in a d--- shame
taken as written
ling is another name for common heather

explanation.surface: A cursed gale ruins the heather on the moor.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting smaller or weaker over time, shrinking away.

clue.text: Skater's catarrh ?

parts.note: a skater works on the ice and might catch a chill there

explanation.surface: A figure skater's runny nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Freezing, as chilly as frozen water; the clue reads it as a chill caught on the rink.

clue.text: " Heads I win " cries the confident candidate

definitions.text: " Heads I win " cries the confident candidate

parts.words: " Heads I win " cries the confident candidate
parts.note: heads is an old word for votes counted, and a confident candidate claims to win the elections

explanation.surface: A coin-toss boast from a cocky election hopeful.
explanation.definitionFit: Heads in the old sense of counted persons, and also votes or elections.

clue.text: Rock singer

parts.note: not a pop musician but the siren of German legend who sang from a cliff over the Rhine

explanation.surface: A rock and roll vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary siren on a Rhine cliff whose song lured boatmen to their deaths.

clue.text: Quill to pluck

parts.note: reads like a feather to be plucked from a bird, but it is a quill used to pluck strings

explanation.surface: A feather ready to be pulled out.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pick, once made of quill, used to pluck the strings of a lute or guitar.

clue.text: Humdrum osculatory measures

parts.note: routine kisses are quick and casual, and the same word names dry measures of two gallons

explanation.surface: Dull kissing tactics.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick perfunctory kisses, and also units of dry capacity of two gallons.

clue.text: One tending towards abstraction

parts.note: sounds like an abstract thinker, but abstraction here is the act of removing things

explanation.surface: Someone inclined to abstract thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who seizes or removes things, abstraction being taking away.

clue.text: Namely I, Clara, in manly Gothic guise

definitions.text: Namely I, Clara, in manly Gothic guise

indicators.note: dressing up as a man and a Goth signals the letters putting on a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A woman named Clara announces that she is disguised as a Gothic man.
explanation.walkthrough: Clara disguised becomes a man of the Goths: the king who sacked Rome in 410.
explanation.definitionFit: The Visigothic king who sacked Rome in AD 410, a man of the Goths.

clue.text: Short address before the organ

annotationWithheld.why: Short address before the organ (4): SLAM; possibly SALAAM shortened, but 'before the organ' has no parse I can confirm

clue.text: No room for more — having stuffed in bars ?

definitions.text: No room for more — having stuffed in bars ?

parts.words: No room for more — having stuffed in bars ?
parts.note: full up after eating chocolate bars, and also crammed with no space left

explanation.surface: Too full to eat another thing after gorging on chocolate.
explanation.definitionFit: Crammed completely, filled to capacity; the clue reads it as full of chocolate.

clue.text: Return to Lerwick lacking oil ignition feed, fond viewer

parts.note: return means go back, so the word go written backwards

indicators.note: lacking means the town's name is without the following part

parts.note: a wick feeds oil to the flame of a lamp

explanation.surface: Instructions for going back to Lerwick in Shetland with no wick to light the lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: Return read as 'go back' gives GO backwards; 'lacking' removes WICK from Lerwick, a town in Shetland, leaving LER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who eyes others amorously, looking with desire.

clue.text: Our Sidney has real potential star quality

definitions.note: a noun phrase standing for an adjective meaning of the stars

parts.note: Sid is the short form of Sidney

indicators.note: potential suggests what the letters could become if rearranged

explanation.surface: Our friend Sidney has genuine promise as a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: An old adjective meaning relating to the constellations, having to do with heavenly bodies.

clue.text: Visionaries hearing sounds of a faulty clock ?

indicators.note: hearing tells us the answer is how the phrase is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a broken clock fails to tick properly, it misses ticks

explanation.surface: Seers who listen to the sound of a broken clock.
explanation.definitionFit: People who seek spiritual truth through contemplation and visions.
